claims.head: The Mammoth should tilt the ice
claims.body: The Mammoth have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Maple Leafs one of the worst. Expect the Mammoth to spend more of the night in the Maple Leafs’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

TOR.head: A tough matchup for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage and gets Tanev back, and Utah will be without Marino, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs can pull it off if their power play gets going.

story.head: The Mammoth should tilt the ice
paras: The Mammoth won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in Utah on Oct 13. The Mammoth (9-5-0) beat Pittsburgh 4-3 in overtime on Thursday, while the Maple Leafs (7-6-2) lost 5-4 to Seattle on Wednesday. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Leafs sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 13th).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.643) says: their chances are worth about .737, and their goaltending has held them back. The Maple Leafs’ record (.533) is about what their chances are worth.

The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd). They also roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), so the Mammoth roll four lines, but the Maple Leafs lean on their top six. As for the Maple Leafs, they get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (30th) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). Toronto has scored 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Mammoth are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs.

Clayton Keller (4 G / 12 A / 16 P in 14 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring. Logan Cooley (7 G / 8 A / 15 P in 14 GP) has a team-high seven goals, with seven points in his last five games. Auston Matthews (10 G / 13 A / 23 P in 15 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is fourth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. William Nylander (9 G / 10 A / 19 P in 15 GP) isn’t far behind.
Karel Vejmelka (6-4-0 / .877 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Utah, and Sergei Bobrovsky (3-5-2 / .885 SV% in 10 GS) for Toronto.
The Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.
